To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
resistance to change of responding in a multiple concurrent schedule was a positive function only of the Pavlovians contingencies when the stimuli were visual but not when the stimuli were auditory.

resistance to change of the response in the presence of the visual stimulus was a positive function (increased) of the Pavlovians contingencies, whereas the resistance to change was not related to the Pavlovian or operant contingencies when the stimulus was auditory.

resistance to change of a response was a positive function (a) of the response-reinforcer contingency when visual stimuli were the discriminative stimuli, and (b) of the stimulus-reinforcer contingency in the presence of auditory stimuli.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of different sensory modalities on the resistance to change of behavior.
the effects of Pavlovian stimuli on behavioral momentum.
the effects of Pavlovian conditioning on operant behavior, and in particular the effects of response-reinforcer and stimulus-reinforcement relationships on behavioral momentum.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effect of Pavloviian contingencies on behavioral momentum depends on the sensory modality of the discriminative stimulus.

resistance to change in the absence of the visual discriminative stimuli is a function of the operant contingencies and the Pavlovian contingency, and resistance to change in extinction in the presence of the auditory discriminative stimuli is determined only by the operant contingencis.
the effect of Pavlorian contingencies is not the same across all sensory modalities, and the role of Pavlorian relations in behavioral momentum may depend on stimulus salience.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effect of operant contingencies upon resistance to change is not affected by the discriminative-stiulus modality.
resistance to change is a function of both operant and Pavlovian contingences.
the effects of Pavlovian relations on resistance to change are modality-specific.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effect of Pavlovanian relations on behavioral momentum is dependent upon the sensory modality of the stimulus.

behavioral momentum is a function of Pavlovian as well as operant relations, and this function may depend on the sensory modality used to signal the response-reinforcer and stimulus-reinforcement relations.
the effect of Pavlovia contingencies on resistance to change is modality specific.
